claim: The formal modelling literature on creator platforms treats it as an established premise that most creators do not earn significant income while a small number of popular creators drive the majority of traffic.
stance_target: Extreme income concentration among creators is a settled assumption in the technical literature, not a contested claim
scope_conditions: Stated as a modelling assumption in an ICLR 2023 theory paper, citing Cheng et al. 2008 on YouTube traffic; no sample size, year, or income figures are attached, and the underlying citation is from 2008
quoted_support: Most creators do not earn significant income, but the majority of traffic is driven by only a few popular and high-earning creators (Cheng et al., 2008).

claim: YouTube creator income arrives through at least nine distinct channels spanning on-platform and off-platform sources, so no single platform payout figure can represent a creator's earnings.
stance_target: Platform-disclosed payout data is structurally incomplete as a measure of creator income
scope_conditions: Taxonomy figure only, drawn from Ormen & Gregersen 2022; no volumes or shares assigned to any channel
quoted_support: income streams direct user payment (Super Chat & Super Stickers) external (off-platform) webshops memberships YouTube Premium ad share merch sponsored content donation services (e.g., PayPal and Patreon) affiliate marketing (sponsored links) (YouTube Partner Programme)

claim: Recommender-system architecture choices determine whether stable equilibria exist among competing creators at all, meaning creator exit pressure is partly a designed property of the platform rather than an emergent market outcome.
stance_target: Platform algorithm design is a causal input to creator attrition
scope_conditions: Mathematical result about exposure games under matrix-factorization and two-tower recommender models; numerical audits run on MovieLens and LastFM simulated data, not on real creators
quoted_support: We prove that seemingly innocuous algorithmic choices—e.g., non-negative vs. unconstrained factorization—significantly affect the existence and character of (Nash) equilibria in exposure games.
